 JAGDISHBHAI ZAVERBHAI PATEL  Versus  STATE OF GUJARAT =========================================================
Appearance:
ARCHITA M PRAJAPATI(8241) for the Applicant(s) No. 1  for the Respondent(s) No. 2 MR J. K. SHAH, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1 =========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE SAMIR J. DAVE  Date : 18/07/2023

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1.

By way of present petition, the petitioner has prayed to transfer the investigation pertaining to FIR bearing C.R. No. 11192061230253 registered with Viramgam Town Police Station, District Ahmedabad, for the offences punishable under sections 306, 498A and 114 of the IPC.

entities.text: Viramgam Town Police Station, District Ahmedabad
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
2. Heard learned advocates for the respective parties.
3. Learned advocate Ms. Archita Prajapati appearing for the petitioner submitted that the victim has died on 17.05.2023 and the reasons for death was shown to be suicide by husband, father-in-law and mother-in-law of the deceased.

Thereafter, the parents of victim though has asked the police officer to investigate into the case of the victim's death, the police officer did not lodge NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/8883/2023 ORDER DATED: 18/07/2023 undefined FIR.

She also submitted Jagdishbhai Zaverbhai Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65690184/
1 that when the incident like suicide or doubtful death is reported and/or the police came to know about such incident, it is the prime duty of the police officer that without permitting the accused person or family members, the police officers are duty bound to take the body to the hospital and request the doctor of government hospital to carry out the postmortem and to record the FIR against such suspicious person and to start investigation.

entities.text: Jagdishbhai Zaverbhai Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She further submitted that the police officer has come to know that this is a case of murder or suicide, they have not requested for postmortem of the body or has not registered the FIR.

She further submitted that the police authority has not proceeded with the investigation pertaining to the said suicide as they have not carried out the postmortem report, no forensic evidence is collected, no panchnama was carried out on the day when the dead body was brought to the hospital.

She also submitted that the police has not recorded the statement of the petitioner and his family members and after number of requests and after petitioner's niece had written letters to the various authorities, then the FIR had been lodged by the police officer of Viramgam Police Station.

She also submitted that the petitioner and his family members are apprehending biased investigation on the part of the investigating NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/8883/2023 ORDER DATED: 18/07/2023 undefined officers.
She therefore requested to transfer the investigation to CBI or CID, Gujarat State for independent investigation of the impugned FIR.

4. Learned APP Mr. J. K. Shah for the respondent- State has resisted this on the ground that the powers under section 482 of Cr.P.C., are to be exercised by the Court sparingly and in an appropriate case at an appropriate time.

Presently, the investigation in this case is going on and it is at a crucial stage and no charge-sheet is filed, and therefore, the complaint may not be transferred.
5.

Having heard learned advocate for the petitioner and learned APP for the respondent State and considering the FIR and other material placed on record, it appears from the FIR that the incident took place on 17.05.2023 and FIR was registered on 27.05.2023.

It appears from the FIR that on 17.05.2023 the petitioner came to know about the incident that his daughter has committed suicide and therefore, he alongwith his family members visited Shaligram Hospital, Viramgam, where he met his son-in-law and they found the dead body of their daughter in the hospital.
It appears that there is no explanation given in the FIR regarding delay of so many days.

It also appears from the FIR that after consultation with the family members and elderly persons from the NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/8883/2023 ORDER DATED: 18/07/2023 undefined society, the petitioner and his wife agreed not to initiate any inquiry or proceeding regarding this incident of suicide looking to the age and future of their grandson and, therefore no postmortem or inquest panchnama of dead body of the deceased has been carried out and cremation of the deceased has been done.
6. It has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of CBI v. Rajesh Gandhi, 1997 Cri LJ 63, that no one can insist that an offence be investigated by a particular agency.

entities.text: CBI v. Rajesh Gandhi, 1997 Cri LJ 63
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I am fully agree with the view in the aforesaid decision.

An aggrieved person can only claim that the offence he alleges be investigated properly, but he has no right to claim that it be investigated by any particular agency of his choice.
Jagdishbhai Zaverbhai Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65690184/
2

entities.text: Jagdishbhai Zaverbhai Patel vs State Of Gujarat
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. The principle of law that emerges from the precedents of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is that the power to transfer an investigation must be used "sparingly" and only "in exceptional circumstances".

In assessing the plea urged by the petitioner that the investigation must be transferred to the CBI, I am guided by the parameters laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court for the exercise of that extraordinary power.

8. Bearing in mind the position of law as discussed above and, in the facts, and circumstances of the NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/8883/2023 ORDER DATED: 18/07/2023 undefined case, this Court is of the opinion that there is no need to transfer the investigation to CBI.
Even the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner has not vehemently pressed such a prayer.
9. In view of the above and for the reasons stated above, no case is made out to entertain the present petition and hence, present petition being devoid of merits stands dismissed.

(SAMIR J. DAVE,J) MEHUL B. TUVAR Jagdishbhai Zaverbhai Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65690184/
